summary: H.R. 435, titled the 'Direct Hire To Fight Fires', provides permanent direct-hire authority to the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior to fill wildland firefighter and firefighting support positions within the Forest Service and Interior agencies. It requires both departments to implement policies that streamline hiring and improve recruitment and retention, and mandates annual reporting on staffing needs, vacancies, and hiring barriers to Congress and the public.

affected_groups.effect: May experience streamlined hiring processes, reduced barriers when transferring between agencies, and easier re-hiring if previously employed by the agencies.
Granted permanent direct-hire authority and required to create new recruitment policies, track vacancy and staffing data, and publish annual reports.
affected_groups.group: Department of Agriculture and Department of the Interior

key_provisions: Grants permanent direct-hire authority to the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior for wildland firefighter and support positions.
Lists specific occupational series eligible for direct hire, such as forestry technicians, aircraft operators, and dispatchers, plus any future series created specifically for wildland firefighting.

Requires policies to be implemented within one year to reduce hiring time, eliminate process redundancies, streamline the re-hiring of former employees, and lower barriers for transferring between agencies.
Requires annual reports to be submitted to relevant congressional committees detailing staffing projections, planned hiring events, current employee counts, and vacancies by state.
Mandates that the annual reports on hiring, vacancies, and implementation progress be published on a public website.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 435, titled the 'Direct Hire To Fight Fires', provides permanent direct-hire authority to the Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior to fill wildland firefighter and firefighting support positions within the Forest Service and Interior agencies. It requires both departments to implement policies that streamline hiring and improve recruitment and retention, and mandates annual reporting on staffing needs, vacancies, and hiring barriers to Congress and the public.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes federal hiring procedures for wildland firefighting personnel in the Forest Service and Department of the Interior by bypassing standard appointment procedures to speed up recruitment and mandating continuous public and congressional oversight of agency staffing needs and vacancies.
